doc.tool: Current state with the agentview (third-person) and wrist images.

doc.code:
TCP position (world: +y away from the robot, +x its right, +z up), gripper width and command, the task's success flags and metrics, the workspace box.

Example:
    st = state()
    print(st["tcp_pos"], st["gripper_width"], st["success"])
    lo, hi = st["workspace"]["min"], st["workspace"]["max"]

height.description: Pixels (default 256, the images shown; 1024 = back_project's high resolution)

doc.tool: Camera calibration (OpenCV intrinsic K and camera-to-world extrinsic) of the agentview or wrist camera at an image size (default 256x256, the images shown).
doc.code:
OpenCV intrinsics and camera-to-world extrinsic of a camera at a resolution.

Example:
    meta = get_camera_meta("agentview")
    K, T = meta["intrinsic_K"], meta["extrinsic_cam2world"]

prompt.description: What to segment, e.g. 'red puck' (or give point)

point.description: A positive point [row, col] instead of a prompt

doc.tool: SAM3 segmentation of the current camera image (256x256 as shown, or 1024 with resolution high). Give exactly one of a text prompt or a positive point [row, col]. The top mask is projected through the depth map; world_xyz is the median over its pixels. Returns an overlay image.
doc.code:
SAM3 mask of a text prompt (or a point [row, col]) in the current image: found, score, box, mask, n_pixels, centroid_pixel [row, col], world_xyz (median of the mask's pixels through the depth).

Example:
    m = segment("red puck")
    if m["found"]:
        print(m["world_xyz"], m["score"])

z_min.description: Region mode: keep pixels with world z >= z_min

z_max.description: Region mode: keep pixels with world z <= z_max

pixels.description: Instead of row/col: [[row, col], ...]; returns a list (None where no depth)

doc.tool: World xyz of a pixel (row, col; row 0 = top) in the current camera image (256x256 as shown, or 1024 with resolution high), from the depth map. Region mode: row_range + col_range (+ optional z_min/z_max) returns the midpoint of world xy over that window, e.g. a container's interior centre.
doc.code:
World xyz of pixel (row, col) of the current image through the depth: {pixel, world_xyz} (error where the depth is invalid). Region mode: row_range + col_range (+ z_min / z_max) returns center_xyz (midpoint of world x and y, median z). pixels=[[row, col], ...] returns a list.

Example:
    print(back_project(128, 140)["world_xyz"])
    bin = back_project(row_range=[90, 130], col_range=[150, 200])["center_xyz"]

gripper.description: Open or close first, holding still (default: keep)

doc.tool: Translate the gripper by a world-frame [dx, dy, dz] in metres (+y away from the robot, +x toward the robot's right, +z up; at most {{max_move}} m per call, inside the workspace box), optionally opening or closing the gripper first (the arm holds still until the fingers settle, then moves). The orientation is fixed. Returns the new state and images.
doc.code:
Translate the gripper by a world-frame delta (m), closed-loop; at most 0.2 m per call and inside the workspace box, else refused. Optionally open or close the gripper first.

Example:
    r = move_delta([0, 0.05, -0.03], gripper="open")
    print(r["final_tcp_pos"], r["final_error_m"])

close.description: true closes and holds, false opens

doc.tool: Open or close the gripper in place and hold until the fingers settle. The command persists across moves. Returns the new state and images.
doc.code:
Close (True) or open (False) the gripper in place and hold until the fingers settle.

Example:
    r = set_gripper(True)
    print(r["gripper_width"])  # about 0.023: closed on nothing

doc.tool: Execute one planned grasp (a g id of the current observation, from plan_grasp) in one call: open to the pre-grasp standoff back along its approach, descend to it, close, lift straight up, each leg as bounded moves. The gripper cannot turn, so only a candidate approaching from (nearly) straight above runs; a tilted one is refused before anything moves. Returns each leg's final_dist_m; stalled when a leg stopped short. The id is spent either way; afterwards plan_place with this grasp_id plans from the held object.
doc.code:
Run one planned grasp id: open at the standoff back along its approach, descend, close, lift, each leg as bounded move_delta calls; refused (nothing moves) unless it approaches from nearly straight above. Returns legs (final_dist_m each), stalled when a leg stopped short.

Example:
    g = plan_grasp("red puck")
    r = execute_grasp(g["active"])
    print(r["legs"], r.get("stalled", False))

doc.tool: Execute one planned place (a p id from plan_place) in one call: carry to the pre-place above it, descend, open, retreat, each leg as bounded moves; refused when its approach is not (nearly) straight down.
doc.code:
Run one planned place id: carry to the pre-place above it, descend, open, retreat, each leg as bounded move_delta calls.

Example:
    r = execute_place(plan_place(region="blue target", grasp_id="g1")["active"])

depth.description: Also return the metric depth map

doc.code:
One camera's RGB frame, and its metric depth map with depth=true.

Example:
    rgb, depth = render_camera("agentview", 256, 256, depth=True)

One action [dx, dy, dz, gripper] in [-1, 1]: 1 cm per unit, +1 closes the gripper.

Example:
    r = step([0, 0, 0.5, -1])  # up 5 mm, gripper open
    print(r["state"]["tcp_pos"], r["success"])

Run actions [N, 4] in one call; stops early at success.

Example:
    r = chunk_step([[0, 1, 0, -1]] * 5)  # 5 cm away from the robot
    print(r["steps"], r["state"]["tcp_pos"])
